blockers.title: [CLOSED in Phase 1D] Coupled scattering amplitude normalisation / null-vector direction accuracy
blockers.detail: CLOSED. The recorded diagnosis was WRONG and is retracted. The null-vector DIRECTION was never the problem: measured against an independent two-sided-equilibrated dps=120 Gram-matrix eigenvector it agrees to better than 1e-40 on all four branches (regression test U3C). The 1.86e-5 energy residual came from two defects in flux_z_mp: (i) D_z built with eps11 instead of eps33, a 13 percent error in the dielectric term that produced 1.8555e-5 exactly; and (ii) the transverse dissipation channel <D_x> omitted, which leaves exactly (k/xi)^2 = 4.67e-8 at 30 degrees. Both are corrected.

blockers.original_diagnosis: The null-vector DIRECTION for the 6mm characteristic matrix (cond ~1e22) is accurate only to ~1e-5. Because the energy balance identity is scale-invariant in the null vector, this residual cannot be a magnitude error. It is the root cause of every coupled R/T/A result being unavailable.

blockers.title: U-5 - factor-of-one-half bookkeeping between mechanical and thermal interface dissipation
blockers.detail: A bookkeeping convention, not a physics uncertainty: the mechanical form carries a 1/2 from the cycle average while the thermal form is written for the real temperature jump. The Phase-2 solver must pick one convention and apply it uniformly before any numerical balance is assembled. Doing it wrong produces a 50 percent error in the thermal channel alone.

blockers.title: Open scientific question: vanishing cycle-averaged time derivative versus vanishing stored-energy term in Lord-Shulman theory
blockers.detail: MATHEMATICAL QUESTION RESOLVED in Phase 1D; PHYSICAL QUESTION REMAINS OPEN, so this blocker is NOT closed. The derivation in theory/energy_flux_derivation.tex sec:ls-closure proves Proposition prop:relax: for a monochromatic field <q.qdot> = 0 IDENTICALLY while <q.q> = |Q|^2/2 is NOT zero, so the vanishing of the first is not evidence about the second. The EIT stored-energy density tau_q q.q/(2 kappa T0) is therefore genuinely non-zero. What remains open is which functional an EXPERIMENT measures, and that requires a complete scattering solution. The original text below is retained unchanged. ORIGINAL: The cycle average of q.dq/dt is IDENTICALLY ZERO for a monochromatic field, because it is the average of a product of a quantity with its own time derivative over a period. Phase 1 treated tau_q q.dq/dt/kappa as a 'relaxation storage' term and then as a dissipation; both readings are unsupported for a monochromatic field, since the term is zero. It is therefore NEITHER storage NOR dissipation in the harmonic regime. Whether Lord-Shulman theory carries a genuine out-of-phase stored-energy contribution, and if so what its correct harmonic expression is, is NOT settled by the observation that this particular term vanishes. Resolving it requires a complete thermodynamic derivation of the LS internal energy, not a numerical test.
blocks: a defensible statement of the LS energy identity in the harmonic regime
blockers.evidence: numeric: 3.27e-6 against a 1e34 dissipation scale, i.e. zero to machine precision

blockers.title: nullspace.null_vector and _rel_residual use an unsound residual metric and are still imported
blockers.detail: `nullspace._rel_residual` divides by the GLOBAL matrix max. The rows of M are equations in different units spanning 1e-5 to 1e19, so a candidate violating the quietest row by 3.6e-5 scores 1.8e-24 and passes. Measured: at Al6061 k=0 on the shear branch the routine returns (0,1,0,-2.16e6) instead of the true (1,0,0,0), at residual 3.0e-7 by its own metric and 4.95e-7 by the row-relative one. `_two_sided_equilibrate` compounds it by lifting a roundoff-level row to unit scale. assembly.py and modal.py now route through scattering/roots.py instead, but the old functions remain because other modules import them. Deleting them is the correct fix and is deferred rather than risked silently.
blocks: a future caller reaching for the convenient-looking API

blockers.title: The phi/Dz removal reason still says 'sagittal decoupling' where the cause is e31=e33=e15=0
blockers.detail: Al6061 is non-piezoelectric, so no admitted mode carries a potential -- the phi and Dz rows are empty because of the MATERIAL, not because of normal incidence. The reduction reaches the right decision and records the wrong reason for part of the basis, and the same wording appears in the earlier normal-incidence write-up. Wording, not mathematics: the PZT cases keep the phi row correctly. TASK 2S UPDATE: the reason wording has been corrected in the Task 2S derivation. At k=0 the phi row is removed because the potential has no finite k=0 value (it diverges like 1/k), and the Dz row because it is the insulated condition; Al6061 additionally carries no potential at all, which remains a separate material fact.
blocks: the traceability of the reduction reason

blockers.title: Transmission magnitudes above unity are unnormalised state amplitudes, not flux coefficients
blockers.detail: The interface system is built from dimensionless STATE vectors of unit component norm, so the incident 'amplitude' is not a unit power flux. Measured transmitted field magnitudes reach 4.3e4 for Al6061|PZT-5H at 30 deg while the system is consistent at 1e-33. Reading these as reflection and transmission coefficients and forming 1-R-T would produce a large spurious negative absorption. No energy quantity may be computed until the incident data is normalised to unit flux and the flux is resolved on both sides. This is a prerequisite for G4, not part of task 2R. TASK 2S UPDATE: the unit-normalisation half of this concern is addressed (per-field row scaling, BLK-02A-20). What remains is the incident-flux normalisation itself, which is still not done and still blocks G4.

blockers.title: Interface continuity rows built from per-side dimensionless states
blockers.detail: Side.states divides each field by THAT medium's own reference scales. For dissimilar media the two sides are then in different units and states1-states2=-incident is not a continuity condition. Scale ratios Al6061 vs PZT-5H at k=0: theta 2.46881, txz 0.738449, tzz 0.597113, qz 178.461, Dz 2.46731e-13, phi 5.58798e-10. Measured consequence for Al|PZT SV at k=0: the production system satisfied its OWN matrix to 2.296e-41 while PHYSICAL traction continuity was violated by 0.2616 (26%). Rebuilding the identical rows from raw physical states gave 8.078e-28 matrix residual and 2.492e-41 physical continuity, with coefficients differing in the third digit.
blockers.resolution: assembly.py builds columns and rhs from raw_states; solver.py reconstructs boundary residuals from raw_states. Physical continuity now 1.2e-41.

blockers.title: Column normalisation by the Euclidean norm over mixed physical units
blockers.detail: With physical columns restored the entries span 1e-37 (Dz) to 1e22 (qz) and the raw system reaches cond 1.6e62; mp.lu_solve raises 'matrix is numerically singular'. Dividing by the Euclidean column norm is not a fix: the norm is dominated by qz, so a column with ux=1 normalises to 1.9e-14 and two columns differing by the shear-modulus ratio 1.066 score a Cauchy-Schwarz overlap of 1.0 -- a false duplicate.

closure_evidence.independent_formulation: diagonal row scaling s_i = max_j |state_i| per field, then diagonal column scaling n_j = max_i |state_i/s_i| per mode; both are invertible so the solution set is unchanged

blockers.title: Rank-gain argument for the normal-incidence row removal is vacuous
blockers.detail: Task 2R removed the phi row because adding it produced zero rank gain. Once rows>=columns and the columns are independent the rank equals the column count whatever the extra row says, so zero gain is guaranteed. Demonstrated by appending an arbitrary row of constants, which also gains zero rank (EQ-02A-GAUGE-03).
blocks: confidence in the Task 2R reduction justification
blockers.resolution: Argument withdrawn. Replacement: k=0 is a LIMIT because the potential of a polynomial mode diverges like 1/k, and the Dz row at k=0 is the INSULATED interface condition, a different physical model from the bonded contact imposed elsewhere. Equivalence then verified directly at k>0 to 1.707e-48.

closure_evidence.independent_formulation: the limit argument is tested by extrapolation in k, an oracle that does not use the k=0 row-removal rule at all
closure_evidence.measured_withdrawal: an arbitrary appended row of constants also gains zero rank (EQ-02A-GAUGE-03), so zero rank gain cannot certify implication
closure_evidence.replacement_result: full and reduced agree to 1.707e-48 across 4 material pairs x {P,SV} x k/k_ac in {1e-2,1e-4} on all gauge-invariant components
closure_evidence.limit_behaviour: first-order approach to the k=0 answer (decade ratios 60 and 12 for Al|PZT P); identical media exact at every k
closure_evidence.executed_regression: EQ-02A-GAUGE-03, GAUGE-04, GAUGE-05 PASS; mutations MR08, MR09, MR10 DETECTED

blockers.detail: Equivalence of the full and reduced formulations was demonstrated at k>0 tending to normal incidence and at the k=0 limit. blockers.title: Electrical interface model is BONDED, and the discarded Dz row is the INSULATED condition
blockers.detail: Recorded as a standing constraint rather than a defect. The system imposes a bonded (shorted) contact: displacements and tractions continuous, potential continuous, normal D free to jump by a surface charge. The Dz row at k=0 is Gauss's law D_z=0, which is the INSULATED (open-circuit) condition. The two are different physical models and must not be combined or interchanged. MR09 keeps the Dz row and is detected by EQ-02A-GAUGE-06 specifically because of this distinction. Any future change to the electrical interface model must be derived and validated separately.
blocks: silent interchange between bonded and insulated models
